payload.description: StorySparkAI is an open-source platform designed for creative minds to generate and share multiple story variations from a single prompt.

payload.text:
👩‍💻 StorySparkAI is an open-source platform designed for creative minds to generate and share multiple story variations from a single prompt. Perfect for writers, creators, and enthusiasts exploring AI-powered storytelling!

## Table of Contents - [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents) - [About 🚀](#about-) - [Features 💪](#features-) - [Local development (monorepo)](#local-development-monorepo) - [Environment variables](#environment-variables) - [Contributing 👨‍💻](#contributing-) - [Contributors 🤝](#contributors-) - [License](#license) - [Support 🙏](#support-) ## About 🚀 - story-spark-ai - [Website](https://storysparkai.vercel.app/) - **`StorySparkAi`** is an open-source platform designed to empower creative minds by generating and showcasing AI-crafted stories from user prompts in a simple, engaging way. - With **`StorySparkAi`**, users can input an idea, explore multiple story variations, save their favorites, and leverage AI analysis to enhance their creative writing journey. ## Features 💪 - **AI-Powered Story Generation**: Create unique stories instantly using advanced AI models. - **Prompt-Based Storytelling**: Simply provide a prompt or idea and watch it come to life. - **Story Bookmarks/History**: Save your favorite generated stories and revisit your past creations. - **AI Analysis Capabilities**: Get AI insights, summaries, and critiques of your stories. - **Creative Writing Assistance**: Overcome writer's block with intelligent suggestions and variations. - **Responsive User Experience**: Enjoy a seamless and beautiful interface across all devices. ### Local development (monorepo) **Prerequisites:** Node.js **18.18+**, npm **9+**, MongoDB URI for the API. 1. **Clone the repository** ```bash git clone https://github.com//story-spark-ai.git cd story-spark-ai ``` 2. **Install dependencies** (single install at the repo root — npm workspaces) ```bash npm install ``` 3. **Environment files** - Copy `backend/.env.example` → `backend/.env` and fill in all values (see [Environment variables](#environment-variables)). - Copy `frontend/.env.example` → `frontend/.env` and set `VITE_BASE_URL` to your API base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:5000/api/v1` when the backend runs on port 5000). Optionally set `VITE_SOCKET_URL` for real-time notifications; the frontend uses your logged-in access token to join the notification room. > Never commit `backend/.env` or `frontend/.env`. Only `.env.example` files belong in git. 4. **First-Time Setup (Admin Seeding)** Before starting the server for the first time, you must create an admin user: ```bash cd backend npx ts-node scripts/seed-admin.ts ``` Make sure `ADMIN_EMAIL` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` are set in your `backend/.env` file. 5. **Run apps** - **Both** (two terminals or one combined process): ```bash npm run dev ``` - **Backend only:** `npm run dev:backend` — API (default port **5000** if `PORT` is unset). - **Frontend only:** `npm run dev:frontend` — Vite dev server on **http://localhost:4001** 6. **Production builds** ```bash npm run build npm run start:backend # requires `npm run build:backend` first npm run start:frontend # serves built static app (preview) ``` ### Deploying on Vercel Use **two** Vercel projects from this monorepo: | Project | Root directory | Example domain | |---------|----------------|----------------| | Frontend | `frontend` | `storysparkai.vercel.app` | | Backend API | `backend` | `apistorysparkai.vercel.app` | **Frontend environment variables** (redeploy after changing): - `VITE_BASE_URL` = `https://.vercel.app/api/v1` - `VITE_SOCKET_URL` = `https://notification-socket-io.onrender.com` (or your own persistent Node host) - Do **not** point `VITE_SOCKET_URL` at your Vercel API URL — Vercel serverless cannot run Socket.IO, which causes endless `/socket.io/` **404** logs. **Backend environment variables:** set `DATABASE_URL`, JWT secrets, AI keys, and `CORS_ORIGINS` including `https://storysparkai.vercel.app`. **Git:** Use a **single** repository root (one `.git` folder). Do not nest another `.git` inside `frontend/` or `backend/`. ### Environment variables After cloning, create your env files from the examples in the repo: ```bash cp backend/.env.example backend/.env cp frontend/.env.example frontend/.env ``` #### Backend (`backend/.env`) | Variable | Required | Description | |----------|----------|-------------| | `DATABASE_URL` | Yes | MongoDB connection string (local or [Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/cloud/atlas)) | | `PORT` | No | API port (default `5000`) | | `NODE_ENV` | No | `development` or `production` | | `CORS_ORIGINS` | No | Comma-separated frontend URLs (e.g. `http://localhost:4001`) | | `SALT_ROUNDS` | Yes | Bcrypt cost factor (e.g. `10`) | | `JWT_SECRET` | Yes | Access token signing secret | | `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` | Yes | Refresh token signing secret | | `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` | Yes | Access token lifetime (e.g. `60d`) | | `JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRES_IN` | Yes | Refresh token lifetime (e.g. `120d`) | | `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Yes | Initial admin password on seed | | `OPEN_AI_KEY` | For OpenAI | [OpenAI API key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) | | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | For Gemini | [Google AI Studio key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) | | `UNSPLASH_KEY_API` | For images | [Unsplash Access Key](https://unsplash.com/developers) | | `UNSPLASH_KEY_API_SECRET` | For images | Unsplash secret | | `VERIFY_EMAIL` | For email | SMTP sender address | | `VERIFY_PASSWORD` | For email | SMTP password or app password | | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | For login with google | https://console.cloud.google.com | | `CORS_ORIGINS` | For resolve cors | #### Frontend (`frontend/.env`) | Variable | Required | Description | |----------|----------|-------------| | `VITE_BASE_URL` | Yes | API base URL, e.g. `http://localhost:5000/api/v1` | | `VITE_SOCKET_URL` | No | Socket.IO URL for real-time notifications (optional) | | `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | Yes | https://console.cloud.google.com | ### Contributing workflow 1. Fork the repository and clone your fork. 2. Create a branch: `git checkout -b your-feature-branch` 3. Install with `npm install` at the repo root, configure `.env` files, then `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, and open a pull request. ## Contributing 👨‍💻 Contributions make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create.
**Any contributions you make are truly appreciated!** ## Contributors 🤝 Thanks to everyone who has helped build **Story Spark AI**. This section updates automatically when `contributors.json` changes. Merges entries from `contributors.json` with [GitHub contributors](https://github.com/ronisarkarexe/story-spark-ai/graphs/contributors).

## Support 🙏 Thank you for contributing to our open-source project! We appreciate your support 🚀
Don't forget to leave a star ⭐

# **Contributing Guidelines** 📄 This documentation contains a set of guidelines to help you during the contribution process. We are happy to welcome all the contributions from anyone willing to improve/add new scripts to this project. Thank you for helping out and remember, **no contribution is too small.**
Please note we have a [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) please follow it in all your interactions with the project.
## **Need some help regarding the basics?🤔** You can refer to the following articles on basics of Git and Github and also contact the Project Mentors, in case you are stuck: - [Forking a Repo](https://help.github.com/en/github/getting-started-with-github/fork-a-repo) - [Cloning a Repo](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/cloning-a-repository) - [How to create a Pull Request](https://opensource.com/article/19/7/create-pull-request-github) - [Getting started with Git and GitHub](https://towardsdatascience.com/getting-started-with-git-and-github-6fcd0f2d4ac6) - [Learn GitHub from Scratch](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/git-and-github-learning-resources)
**1.** Fork [this](https://github.com/ronisarkarexe/story-spark-ai.git) repository. **2.** Clone your forked copy of the project. ``` git clone https://github.com//story-spark-ai.git ``` **3.** Navigate to the project directory :file_folder: . ``` cd story-spark-ai ``` **4.** Add a reference(remote) to the original repository. ``` git remote add upstream https://github.com/ronisarkarexe/story-spark-ai.git ``` **5.** Check the remotes for this repository. ``` git remote -v ``` **6.** Always take a pull from the upstream repository to your main branch to keep it at par with the main project (updated repository). ``` git pull upstream main ``` **7.** Create a new branch. ``` git checkout -b ``` **8.** Perform your desired changes to the code base. **9.** Track your changes:heavy_check_mark: . ``` git add . ``` **10.** Commit your changes . ``` git commit -m "Relevant message" ``` **11.** Push the committed changes in your feature branch to your remote repo. ``` git push -u origin ``` **12.** To create a pull request, click on `compare and pull requests`. **13.** Add appropriate title and description to your pull request explaining your changes and efforts done. **14.** Click on `Create Pull Request`.
### Alternatively contribute using GitHub Desktop 1. **Open GitHub Desktop:** Launch GitHub Desktop and log in to your GitHub account if you haven't already. 2. **Clone the Repository:** - If you haven't cloned the story-spark-ai repository yet, you can do so by clicking on the "File" menu and selecting "Clone Repository." - Choose the story-spark-ai repository from the list of repositories on GitHub and clone it to your local machine. 3. **Switch to the Correct Branch:** - Ensure you are on the branch that you want to submit a pull request for. - If you need to switch branches, you can do so by clicking on the "Current Branch" dropdown menu and selecting the desired branch. 4. **Make Changes:** Make your changes to the code or files in the repository using your preferred code editor. 5. **Commit Changes:** - In GitHub Desktop, you'll see a list of the files you've changed. Check the box next to each file you want to include in the commit. - Enter a summary and description for your changes in the "Summary" and "Description" fields, respectively. Click the "Commit to " button to commit your changes to the local branch. 6. **Push Changes to GitHub:** After committing your changes, click the "Push origin" button in the top right corner of GitHub Desktop to push your changes to your forked repository on GitHub. 7. **Create a Pull Request:** - Go to the GitHub website and navigate to your fork of the story-spark-ai repository. - You should see a button to "Compare & pull request" between your fork and the original repository. Click on it. 8. **Review and Submit:** - On the pull request page, review your changes and add any additional information, such as a title and description, that you want to include with your pull request. - Once you're satisfied, click the "Create pull request" button to submit your pull request. 9. **Wait for Review:** Your pull request will now be available for review by the project maintainers. They may provide feedback or ask for changes before merging your pull request into the main branch of the story-spark-ai repository. ⭐️ Support the Project If you find this project helpful, please consider giving it a star on GitHub! Your support helps to grow the project and reach more contributors. ## **Issue Report Process 📌** 1. Go to the project's issues. 2. Give proper description for the issues. 3. Don't spam to get the assignment of the issue 😀. 4. Wait until someone is looking into it ! 5. Start working on issue only after you got assigned that issue 🚀.
However, it's important to adhere to strict regulations to maintain the integrity of our contributor records: 1. Only Add Your Details: You are allowed to add your own details to the ContributorsData.ts file. This helps us accurately attribute contributions to the right individuals. 2. Respect Others' Details: Modifying or tampering with existing contributor details is strictly prohibited. Any unauthorized changes may result in your PR not being merged or accepted. We understand that open source collaboration is filled with excitement and fulfillment. Your contributions are invaluable, and we're committed to ensuring that your efforts are duly recognized and appreciated. ## **Pull Request Process 🚀** 1. Ensure that you have self reviewed your code 😀 2. Make sure you have added the proper description for the functionality of the code 3. Ensure you have commented your code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas. 4. Add screenshots — they help in the review process. 5. Submit your PR by giving the necessary information in PR template and hang tight we will review it really soon 🚀
# **Thank you for contributing💗**

Kindly review this PR and merge it if the backend fix looks good.

payload.author: eshaanag
payload.body:
Rechecked this after rebasing the branch on the latest `main`.

Current status:

- `lint` is passing
- `typecheck` is passing
- the PR is mergeable with no conflicts
- the only remaining failing check is `CI / build`

The build job is failing before project dependencies install or any app code runs:

```text
Unable to locate executable file: pnpm
```

That comes from `.github/workflows/main.yml`, where `actions/setup-node` is configured with `cache: pnpm`, but the workflow does not install pnpm first and then runs `npm install` afterward. So the current failure is in the CI setup, not in `backend/src/app/modules/comment/comment.service.ts`.

I kept this PR scoped to the comment service fix for #1652. If maintainers want, I can handle the workflow setup separately, but I did not want to mix a CI workflow change into this bugfix PR without review.

payload.body:
hi @ronisarkarexe ## Summary
Resolves #932

### Changes Made

**Backend:**
- Added `genre?: string` to `IAIModel` interface
- Added `GENRE_MODIFIER_INSTRUCTIONS` map with 6 genres (Fantasy, Horror, Romance, Sci-Fi, Mystery, Children's)
- Added `buildGenreInstruction()` function in `ai_model.utils.ts`
- Genre style directive is injected into the Gemini system prompt before story generation
- `genre` flows through `normalizeStoryPayload` → both authenticated and free generation paths
- Fixed pre-existing file corruption in `story_version.service.ts`

**Tests:**
- Added `genre.constants.test.js` with 6 unit tests — all passing ✅

### How It Works
When a user selects a genre (e.g. Horror), the backend prepends:
> *"Genre & Style Directive: Write in the style of psychological horror. Build dread slowly, use dark imagery, and leave an unsettling feeling."*

...to the Gemini prompt before generation, giving the AI strong stylistic direction.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Genre selector renders with 6 options
- [x] Selected genre visually highlighted
- [x] Genre selection is optional (defaults to no modifier)
- [x] Genre passed to backend in request payload
- [x] Backend injects correct genre modifier into system prompt
- [x] Unit tests cover modifier map and injection logic

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. This PR appears to introduce widespread changes across the frontend and backend, primarily adding `eslint-disable` directives, replacing typed code with `any`, removing meaningful logic, and stubbing out functions. Several files have had real implementations replaced with no-ops or placeholder values, which strongly suggests the changes are masking type/lint errors rather than fixing them. **Changes:** - Replaces typed interfaces and functions with `any` and stub implementations across multiple frontend components. - Removes substantial business logic (Razorpay payment flow, community spotlight ranking, guidelines page, FAQ accordion behavior). - Backend changes include router import path changes, regex helpers, crypto-based room ID generation, and edits to a compiled `dist/` file. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 25 out of 28 changed files in this pull request and generated 18 comments.

Hey admins! Just a quick heads up on this PR.

The original issue for syncing the pnpm-lock.yaml was resolved quickly. However, I noticed that the CI was still failing on the Lint and Type Check jobs because the main branch currently has a lot of broken code that was recently merged (over 60 TypeScript/build errors across the frontend and backend, including broken middleware imports, undefined router variables in App.tsx, and half-finished variables in payment and CollabHome).

Instead of just leaving the CI red or disabling the type-checker, I went ahead and cleanly patched all of the upstream TypeScript and ESLint errors across both the frontend and backend.

The Build, Lint, and Type Check CI workflows should now be 100% green again for everyone! Feel free to review the extra commits, and let me know if you'd like any adjustments.

@ronisarkarexe A quick note on the three red checks (CI/build, Lint, Type Check): they originate from the base branch, not from this change.

- Type Check and CI install fail at the `npm ci` / install step because the committed lockfile is out of sync with `package.json` (for example `helmet`, `express-rate-limit`, `ioredis`, and a `node-cron` version bump are missing from the lock file). This is already tracked in #1161 and #1534.
- CI build also hits pre-existing TypeScript errors in files this PR does not touch, for example `src/app.ts` and `recommendation.service.ts`. These are covered by #1220, #1544, and #1546.
- Lint reports unused-variable and similar errors in components this PR does not touch.

This PR only adds the payment module files and updates `payment.controller.ts`. The same three checks are red on `main` itself, so they are not caused by this change, and "No conflicts with base branch" is green. The merge from upstream has already been done. Happy to rebase once the base-branch CI issues above are resolved.

@ronisarkarexe A quick note on the three red checks (CI/build, Lint, Type Check): they originate from the base branch, not from this change.

- Type Check and CI install fail at the `npm ci` / install step because the committed lockfile is out of sync with `package.json` (for example `helmet`, `express-rate-limit`, `ioredis`, and a `node-cron` version bump are missing from the lock file). This is already tracked in #1161 and #1534.
- CI build also hits pre-existing TypeScript errors in files this PR does not touch, for example `src/app.ts` and `recommendation.service.ts`. These are covered by #1220, #1544, and #1546.
- Lint reports unused-variable and similar errors in components this PR does not touch (App.tsx and others).

This PR only changes `auth.service.ts` and `auth.controller.ts`. The same three checks are red on `main` itself, so they are not caused by this change, and "No conflicts with base branch" is green. Happy to rebase once the base-branch CI issues above are resolved.

payload.author: aishwary-vansh
payload.body: ## Fix build errors & resolve merge conflicts This PR resolves Git merge conflicts from the latest upstream sync and fixes the resulting build errors across the project. **Frontend Fixes:** * **`nav_list.component.tsx`:** Resolved merge conflicts by keeping the cleaner upstream version. It correctly uses the real `auth.service`, dynamic routing, and proper mobile menu components instead of the local placeholder stubs. * **`stories.component.tsx`:** Fixed a TypeScript error in the translation dictionary by changing an invalid Korean object key (`최근 프롬프트:`) back to the correct English variable name (`recentPrompts:`). **Backend Fixes:** * **`reaction.service.ts`:** Resolved merge conflicts in the `toggleReaction` function. Kept the upstream version because it correctly updates the `likesCount` and `reactions` array on the Post document when a reaction is added or removed. * **`auth.controller.ts`:** Fixed a structural error where `changePassword` and `forgotPassword` were accidentally merged into one function. Restored them as two separate, working handlers. * **`auth.router.ts`:** Removed a duplicate import for the IP rate limiter and fixed a missing closing bracket `);` on the change-password route. * **`auth.service.ts`:** Added a missing closing brace `};` to the `changePassword` function that was swallowed during the merge. Both frontend and backend now build successfully with 0 errors. ##Screenshot

payload.body:
## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. This PR focuses on front-end bundle/performance optimizations and UI polish by introducing route/component lazy-loading, build-time chunk splitting, and moving shared i18n/constants and animations into centralized locations. **Changes:** - Add Vite build optimizations (manual chunk splitting, deps pre-bundling controls, prod console/debugger stripping). - Introduce route/component lazy-loading with a Suspense `PageLoader` fallback and additional UI/animation performance improvements. - Extract stories i18n/constants into a dedicated module and move per-render CSS animations to global styles. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 14 out of 15 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | frontend/vite.config.ts | Adds production-oriented build optimizations, chunk splitting, and optimizeDeps tuning. | | frontend/src/services/auth.service.ts | Adjusts token decode typing before building `AuthUserInfo`. | | frontend/src/index.css | Moves fonts to HTML, adds global animation tokens, and refines hover/`will-change` usage. | | frontend/src/components/stories/stories.view.component.tsx | Lazy-loads heavy modals and jsPDF; memoizes component and callbacks. | | frontend/src/components/stories/stories.i18n.ts | New centralized languages/genres/UI text module. | | frontend/src/components/stories/stories.component.tsx | Imports i18n module and updates prompt UI styling/behavior. | | frontend/src/components/post/post.component.tsx | Memoizes derived tags list from fetched posts. | | frontend/src/components/loading/PageLoader.tsx | New Suspense fallback loader UI. | | frontend/src/components/hero/nav_list.component.tsx | Refactors nav into a full component with scroll-based header styling. | | frontend/src/components/hero/hero_section.component.tsx | Performance tweaks (rAF throttling, pausing GSAP offscreen, cleanup improvements). | | frontend/src/components/collab/CollabRoom.tsx | Changes Socket.IO usage to emit on the base socket. | | frontend/src/components/collab/CollabHome.tsx | Same Socket.IO change for room creation. | | frontend/src/App.tsx | Converts many routes to lazy-loaded components and adds Suspense fallback. | | frontend/index.html | Adds SEO/OG/Twitter meta and non-blocking font loading. |

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body: ## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. Closes a rate-limit bypass where clients could spoof the `X-Forwarded-For` header to get a new bucket per request. The middleware now relies solely on `req.ip` (derived from the trusted proxy chain) as the fallback key. **Changes:** - Removed direct `X-Forwarded-For` header parsing from the rate-limit key derivation. - Added explanatory comment documenting the security rationale and dependency on `trust proxy`. - Added test coverage verifying that spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` headers do not create separate buckets. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | backend/src/middlewares/rateLimitMiddleware.ts | Drops untrusted header lookup; key now uses user id → `req.ip` → "anonymous". | | backend/src/__tests__/rateLimitMiddleware.test.ts | Extends `buildMocks` to accept headers and adds two tests covering the spoofing scenario. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.
